cy3.display_name: Cy3 (Cyanine3; sulfoindocyanine, the sulfonated form of 1,1'-diethyl-3,3,3',3'-tetramethylindocarbocyanine)
cy3.notes: The name Cy3 covers two closely related dyes that differ by a few nm: the commercial sulfoindocyanine Cy3 (Cytiva/GE Amersham, Thermo, Lumiprobe, Interchim) and its unsulfonated parent indocarbocyanine (DiIC3; PhotochemCAD K10, in methanol). Reported maxima cluster tightly: absorption 550 nm (Cytiva spec sheet), 554-555 nm (Thermo selection guide, FPbase, Lumiprobe, Interchim), 548 nm (sulfo-Cy3), 544.25 nm (parent indocarbocyanine in methanol, PhotochemCAD); emission 570 nm (Cytiva, Interchim, Lumiprobe), 566 nm (Thermo, FPbase), 563 nm (sulfo-Cy3). Spread: absorption 544-555 nm, emission 563-570 nm, so the 550/570 nm pair is the standard vendor value and is safe to keep. QUANTUM YIELD is the single most environment-sensitive number: 0.04 for the free dye in water/PBS (the value used in the cyanine photophysics literature), 0.07 for the same chromophore in methanol (PhotochemCAD, measured), >0.15 for Cy3/protein conjugates (Cytiva states >0.15 for labelled protein at D/P = 2), 0.10 for sulfo-Cy3 (Lumiprobe) and 0.15 for di-sulfo-Cy3 (Interchim), and 0.31 for the non-sulfonated Cy3 NHS ester (Lumiprobe and Interchim both quote 0.31). So 0.04 describes the free dye in buffer and 0.15-0.31 describes a conjugate or a low-polarity environment; the class value 0.04 is defensible only with the 'free dye in PBS' label. EXTINCTION COEFFICIENT: 150,000 M-1cm-1 (Cytiva spec sheet; the same sheet uses 150,000 at 552 nm in its D/P formula), 150,000 (Lumiprobe, Interchim), 162,000 for sulfo-Cy3 (Lumiprobe, Interchim, and a 2024 peer-reviewed paper that uses 162,000 at 548 nm), 136,000 (FPbase), 133,000 for the parent indocarbocyanine in methanol (PhotochemCAD, scaled to the Sims 1974 literature value). pH: Cy3 conjugates are described as pH-insensitive over about pH 4-10 (Lumiprobe/GoldBio product literature). Environmental sensitivity: fluorescence is quenched by cis-trans photoisomerisation and by dye-DNA/protein stacking, so quantum yield, lifetime and maxima all move with viscosity, binding and solvent; a red shift of about +6 nm absorption is seen when the dye is placed in a more hydrophobic/non-aqueous environment (e.g. 543 nm in PBS for the free dye vs 549 nm in water with 0.25% Tween-20, and 544.25 nm in methanol). DIGITIZED CURVES: digitized_absorption = FPbase 'Cy3' absorption record (450-590 nm), digitized_emission = its emission record (514-670 nm). Both are normalized to their own maximum = 1.0 (relative units; no absolute scale). The absorption shape shows the normal cyanine vibronic shoulder at ~520 nm at roughly half the peak height. A fully documented alternative pair with absolute molar-extinction units measured in methanol is in /tmp/plsim-data/raw/016-abs.txt and 016-ems.txt (PhotochemCAD 2.1a record K10 / OMLC 016: absorption peak 544.25 nm, FWHM 53.9 nm; emission peak 557 nm, FWHM 40.7 nm). FWHM method: measured on the digitized curve supplied in this file at half of its maximum, using the outermost half-maximum crossings (a vibronic shoulder above 50% counts as part of the band), linearly interpolated between 1 nm samples; see SOURCES.md.

cy5.display_name: Cy5 (Cyanine5; sulfoindocyanine, the sulfonated form of 1,1'-diethyl-3,3,3',3'-tetramethylindodicarbocyanine)
cy5.quantum_yield_solvent: PBS buffer / water, free dye (0.28 is the value cited for Cy5 in aqueous solution; individual measurements span 0.19-0.30, see notes)
cy5.notes: As with Cy3, the name covers the commercial sulfoindocyanine Cy5 and its unsulfonated parent indodicarbocyanine (DiIC5; PhotochemCAD K11, in methanol). Absorption maxima reported: 649 nm (Cytiva spec sheet), 646-647 nm (Lumiprobe, Interchim, Thermo selection guide, sulfo-Cy5), 644 nm (FPbase record), 637.5 nm (parent indodicarbocyanine in methanol, PhotochemCAD), 641-647 nm for free vs sulfonated dye measured in PBS (Fan et al. 2023). Emission maxima: 670 nm (Cytiva), 662 nm (Lumiprobe, Interchim), 665-666 nm (Thermo, Tocris), 668 nm (FPbase), 662-670 nm reported elsewhere. Spread: absorption 638-652 nm, emission 662-670 nm. QUANTUM YIELD: 0.28 is the value cited for Cy5 in aqueous solution in the peer-reviewed literature (a 2025 open-access paper, quoting Klehs et al. 2014 ChemPhysChem, gives 'Cy5 ... 0.28 in aqueous solution'), and the Interchim cyanine datasheet gives 0.28 for Cy5 derivatives. Other current values: 0.27 (Lumiprobe's own table), 0.30 (published abstract of Fan et al. 2023 for Cy5 in non-viscous aqueous solution, and FPbase). Direct aqueous measurements are lower: 0.19 has been measured for Cy5 in water, and Tocris quotes 0.20 for Cyanine 5 SE. So 0.28 is a fair central value but the honest range is 0.19-0.30, and the number moves with solvent viscosity, DNA/protein conjugation and photoisomerisation. In methanol the values disagree: PhotochemCAD K11 lists 0.4 for the parent dye (relative measurement, 1995), while a 2026 absolute integrating-sphere measurement gives 0.17 +/- 0.01 for unsubstituted Cy5 in methanol, so the PhotochemCAD 0.4 should be treated with caution (their extinction coefficient, 2.0e5, does agree with that paper's 1.96e5). EXTINCTION COEFFICIENT: 250,000 M-1cm-1 (Cytiva spec sheet; the same sheet uses 250,000 at 650 nm in its D/P formula), 250,000 (Lumiprobe non-sulfonated, Interchim, FPbase, Tocris), 271,000 for sulfo-Cy5 (Lumiprobe, Interchim, and a 2024 peer-reviewed paper measuring it in PBS), 200,000 for the parent indodicarbocyanine in methanol (PhotochemCAD K11, scaled to the Waggoner 1989 value). pH: cyanine conjugates are commonly described as pH-insensitive between about pH 4 and pH 10. Ionic strength matters: absorption maxima of sCy3/sCy5 shift about 1 nm bathochromically and the extinction coefficients rise slightly with added salt, and a DMSO-rich environment shifts them similarly (PMC11721635). DIGITIZED CURVES: digitized_absorption = FPbase 'Cy5' absorption record (430-734 nm, peak 652 nm with the characteristic shoulder near 610 nm), digitized_emission = its emission record (622-734 nm, peak 668 nm). Both normalized to their own maximum = 1.0. FPbase does not state provenance for this dye record, and its own absorption peak (652 nm) sits 8 nm red of its reported excitation maximum (644 nm); the vendor consensus maximum is 646-649 nm. A documented alternative measured in methanol with absolute extinction units is in /tmp/plsim-data/raw/017-abs.txt and 017-ems.txt (PhotochemCAD 2.1a record K11 / OMLC 017: absorption peak 637.5 nm, FWHM 39.2 nm; emission peak 657 nm, FWHM 38.5 nm). FWHM method: measured on the digitized curve supplied in this file at half of its maximum, using the outermost half-maximum crossings (a vibronic shoulder above 50% counts as part of the band), linearly interpolated between 1 nm samples; see SOURCES.md.

methylene-blue.display_name: Methylene blue (methylthioninium chloride, C16H18ClN3S, MW 319.85; a thiazine/phenothiazine dye)
methylene-blue.quantum_yield_solvent: water (aqueous solution); 0.04 in ethanol (see notes for the 0.02-0.05 spread)
methylene-blue.notes: ABSORPTION MAXIMUM: 664 nm is the value attached to the measured water spectrum used here (PhotochemCAD PSW009, whose stated reference is JACS Au, DOI 10.1021/jacsau.5c01463) and it is also the peak of Prahl's independent water measurement (OMLC) and the monomer band maximum obtained by deconvolution of concentration series (ACS Omega 2020: monomer 664 nm, dimer 607 nm, tetramer 600 nm). The Merck Index (quoted on the OMLC page) instead lists 'peak absorption at 668 and 609 nm', i.e. 664-668 nm for the main band plus the ~609-610 nm dimer/higher-aggregate shoulder. So 664 nm is a safe value for a dilute aqueous sample and 668 nm for the literature/excitation maximum; in ethanol the maximum moves to 656 nm (PhotochemCAD I12). EMISSION MAXIMUM: 685 nm measured in water (PhotochemCAD PSW009 emission data); 686 nm is the commonly quoted literature value and differs from the measurement only by the 1 nm sampling. In ethanol the emission maximum is 677 nm (PhotochemCAD I12). QUANTUM YIELD: methylene blue is a very weak fluorophore. 0.02 is the value used for MB in water as a reference dye in the photodynamic-therapy literature (2025 peer-reviewed paper: 'increased fluorescence quantum yields in aqueous media (4-13%) compared with MB (2%)'; a 2022 J. Fluoresc. paper likewise uses Phi_f = 0.02 for MB in water). A measured value in ethanol is 0.04 (PhotochemCAD I12, Taniguchi & Lindsey 2018), and values of 'about 0.04' are also quoted for water in the photosensitiser literature. Honest range for water: 0.02-0.04 (some sources give up to 0.05). The class value 0.04 corresponds to the ethanol measurement or to the loosely quoted 'about 0.04'; if the simulator models an aqueous sample, 0.02 is the better-grounded number, and the difference is entirely inside the reported spread. EXTINCTION COEFFICIENT: the number depends strongly on what is being measured. (a) 67,000 M-1cm-1 at 664 nm is the value the source database assigns to the measured water spectrum reproduced here; (b) 74,000 M-1cm-1 at 664 nm is the peak of Prahl's independent 10 microM aqueous measurement (OMLC tabulated data); (c) 107,800 M-1cm-1 at 664 nm is the intrinsic monomer extinction coefficient obtained by deconvoluting the monomer/dimer/tetramer equilibria (ACS Omega 2020) - this is the true monomer value and is at the top of the range because a real dilute solution always contains some dimer. So a model that assumes monomer-only Beer-Lambert absorbance should use ~1.08e5, while a model that reproduces a real measured cuvette spectrum should use the 6.7e4-7.4e4 apparent value. The 95,000 M-1cm-1 often quoted in the literature sits between the two; I could not find a citable primary source for it, so it is not reported as a value here. SOLVENT / pH / CONCENTRATION DEPENDENCE: the visible band is a monomer band with a shoulder at about 609-610 nm from the dimer; raising concentration or ionic strength, or lowering temperature, increases the fraction of dimer and shifts intensity toward 607-610 nm (dimer) and 600 nm (tetramer), which is why apparent extinction coefficients and apparent quantum yields vary so much between reports. The dimerisation constant itself could not be verified from any source I was able to read (the relevant Spectrochim. Acta A 2019 study is paywalled), and the pH dependence of the band was not verified either - treat both as unsourced background. DIGITIZED CURVES: digitized_absorption = PhotochemCAD PSW009 absorption data in water (300-800 nm, 501 points), digitized_emission = its emission data in water (625-850 nm, 226 points). Both normalized to their own maximum = 1.0 (the absorption file is distributed already normalized: value 1.0000 at 664 nm; the emission file likewise, maximum at 685 nm). The absorption curve is a real measured spectrum of a real (partly aggregated) aqueous sample, not a monomer-only curve: its blue edge, which in more concentrated or more aggregated samples develops into the 607-610 nm dimer band, sits at 0.44 of the peak at 610 nm (0.51 in the OMLC data set). Alternative water data with absolute extinction units are in /tmp/plsim-data/raw/ombc_mb.txt (OMLC, 200-800 nm, peak 74,028 M-1cm-1 at 664 nm); alternative ethanol data are in /tmp/plsim-data/raw/I12_abs.txt and I12_ems.txt (PhotochemCAD I12: absorption 656 nm, FWHM 42.2 nm, epsilon 40,700; emission 677 nm, FWHM 50.5 nm, quantum yield 0.04). FWHM method: measured on the digitized curve supplied in this file at half of its maximum, using the outermost half-maximum crossings (a vibronic shoulder above 50% counts as part of the band), linearly interpolated between 1 nm samples; see SOURCES.md.
